name: Juice Bar
notes: Work-list name 'Juice Bar' matches address exactly (909 Grand Ave, San Diego) to 'Bahia Mexican Food & PB Juice Bar' -- a combined Mexican-food/juice-bar business at that address (prior tenant at same address, Shakeaway, is permanently closed per Yelp). No independent restaurant website. Sourced from the DoorDash marketplace listing's schema.org Menu JSON-LD (server-rendered, no browser needed). Markup check passed: dividing by 1.2/1.15/1.1/1.04 gave at most 28.6% clean-cent landings (1.2), well short of the ~75-100% signature of a real markup, and prices are POS-style odd cents ($8.10, $11.40, $17.40) consistent with a real menu, not a divisor. Captured all 16 menu sections on the listing: Most Ordered, Tortas (x2), Seafood Appetizers, Fruit Salad, Soups & Salads, Salads, Seafood Soups, Seafood Cocktails, Chimichangas, Enchiladas, Combos, Quesadillas, More Delicious Food, Burritos, Seafood Platter -- this is a complete Mexican-food menu. However the 'PB Juice Bar' half of the business (smoothies, tropical/green juice, wraps, acai berry bowls) is NOT represented beyond a single 'Acai Bowl small $8.50' in Most Ordered -- the delivery listing evidently does not carry that side of the menu for online ordering. Grubhub and Uber Eats listings for the same business are client-rendered JS shells and returned no data via curl; Yelp 403s curl. This is the best available source; the juice/smoothie side of the menu could not be confirmed priced anywhere reachable without a browser.

name: La Gran Terraza
notes: Restaurant is O'Toole's / La Gran Terraza, University of San Diego's on-campus fine-dining room, at 5998 Alcala Park Way -- matches work list address exactly (menu header reads 'UNIVERSITY OF SAN DIEGO'). Own Wix site (lagranterraza.com) links 4 first-party PDF menus directly in the page HTML. pdftotext -layout scrambled/dropped many prices where the PDF used a small dot-separator glyph instead of extractable text, so both food PDFs were read visually with the Read tool (per playbook) rather than trusted from pdftotext -- recovered soup cup/bowl prices, salad add-on prices, and the full beverage list that pdftotext had silently dropped. Two food PDFs (Lunch; and the Shareables/Salads/Plates dinner menu, labelled 'O'Toole's La Gran Terraza') overlap heavily (same salads, same add-on prices, several shared entrees at identical prices) -- treated as one cross-check: every overlapping dish/price matched exactly between the two documents, so duplicates were recorded once. A third PDF (Beer/Wine list) was also read visually and its numbers (which pdftotext rendered with no '$' at all) are real per-item prices printed on the document -- included as Beer and Wine sections. The draft-beer price grid ($7 12oz / $8 16oz / $24 pitcher) is a flat rate across all listed taps, not a per-beer price, and is recorded as three generic 'Local Draft Beer' rows rather than fabricating a price per beer name; each tap beer this rate covers is named in that row's description. A fourth PDF ('Summer 2026 Special Event Menus') is a private-event/catering/buffet packet -- excluded as an adjunct, not the walk-in menu. Categories reached: Lunch (Soups, Salads, Entrees, Desserts, Beverages), Shareables, Plates, Dinner Desserts, Dinner Beverages, Beer (draft + bottled/canned), Wine (by the glass + by the bottle). Categories not reached / excluded: the private-event catering PDF (adjunct, by design).

Restaurant's own NetWaiter storefront (donluciostacoshopii.netwaiter.com, address and phone both confirmed matching) exists but its menu lives behind a client-rendered my.netwaiter.com SPA with zero prices in server HTML - not used. A WebSearch summary independently surfaced several of the same prices verbatim (Burrito $5.94, Steak Con Huevo $6.45, Egg & Cheese Burrito $2.75), consistent with this being the live listing rather than a stale or altered one. Price level (tacos $2.45-$3.45, burritos $4.50-$8.75) is low for 2026 generally but plausible for this specific old-school taco shop, per multiple reviews describing it as a longtime cheap hole-in-the-wall.
